# Phase 19: a multi-turn evaluation

Item 4 of the [gap table](../GAP_TABLE.md)'s recommended order, first half. Every quality test
before this phase was single-turn: one prompt, one short answer, so the KV a policy managed was
almost entirely the prompt. Gap table item A5 (a working-set-aware selector that protects recent
history) is motivated by a failure only a conversation can show, and the gap table says the
evaluation has to exist before A5 is built. Questions, the decision rule for A5 and the viability
rule were fixed in `configs/phase19.yaml` before any run, including the smoke test, whose output is
not reported.

## What was built

- `lazykv/multiturn.py`: **multi-turn retrieval sessions.** A document of exactly
  32,768 tokens with four doc needles (RULER's multi-key NIAH
  needles at 10, 35, 60 and 85% depth, which needle sits where varying by session), then
  8 turns in total. Each turn after the first
  pastes a passage from a different book (so the conversation grows by real text, as a document chat
  does), may introduce a **chat needle** ("Also note: one of the special magic numbers for X is: N."),
  and asks one question. The schedule is fixed: doc needles are each asked once; three chat needles
  are each asked 2 or 3 turns after they are given; the last turn re-asks the turn-0 doc needle, whose
  answer is by then also in the conversation. Turn 0 is the single-turn NIAH multi-key question
  verbatim.
- **How a session is fed.** Every token after the document goes through the decode path one token
  at a time, under every policy. The tier is decode-only, and rung 5 attends densely to a
  multi-token forward, so feeding a user turn as one chunk would give rung 5 an attention the tier
  cannot have. The model's answers are its own greedy output, so each policy follows its own
  conversation; later turns are paired by position in the schedule, not by identical context.
- **Budgets** are fractions of the session's planned length (document, every fed turn, and the
  answer allowance per turn), so K blocks are fixed for the session. The conversation added a median of
  1,811 tokens to the document.
- `scripts/08_multiturn.py`, `scripts/analyze_phase19.py`. Tests (`tests/test_multiturn.py`): the
  document has exact length and every needle where recorded; chat needles never appear in the
  document and are always given before they are asked; the KV length after a session is exactly the
  document plus the fed turns plus the answers (the end-of-turn token is never fed twice); and over a
  session that seals blocks mid-conversation, the tier answers every turn token for token as rung 5.

## The run

Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, 20 sessions, 64-token blocks, the
quality kernel. Conditions: the full cache, window + sink (rung 2) and Quest-style selection
(rung 5) at 12.5% and 6.25%, and the CPU tier (rung 6) at 6.25% as a validity check. Conditions ran
in a shuffled order per session, each from the same document prefill.

### Question 1: A5's premise

| Budget | Rung 5 chat retention | Its 95% CI upper bound | Window chat retention | Failure observed (config rule) |
| --: | --: | --: | --: | --- |
| 12.5% | 58.3% | 71.7% | 100.0% | **yes** |
| 6.25% | 25.0% | 36.7% | 100.0% | **yes** |

- **The failure A5 is meant to fix is observed, at both budgets, under the rule fixed beforehand.** On
  chat-needle turns, rung 5 keeps 58.3% of
  the full cache's score at 12.5% and 25.0%
  at 6.25%; the window keeps all of it. The full cache answers
  100.0% of chat-needle turns, so the task is viable.
- **The document fails too, which A5 would not fix.** At 6.25%, rung 5 answers
  70.0% of doc questions at turn 0 and
  23.3% at later turns. The window answers no
  doc question at any turn: it holds the conversation, not the document.
- **Rung 6 is rung 5.** The CPU tier gave rung 5's answer text on
  160 of 160
  turns, with blocks sealed into the tier mid-conversation.

### Post hoc: the loss is in reading the user's turn, not in answering

Decided after four sessions of the main run and labelled as such (`configs/phase19.yaml`, amendment).
Same sessions, rung 5 only, with each user turn fed in one dense forward and only the answers decoded
sparsely, which is what every single-turn test did.

| Budget | Questions | Turns | Rung 5, turns fed per token | Rung 5, turns fed densely | Dense better / worse | Sign test p | Dense-turn retention (95% CI) |
| --: | --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| 12.5% | Chat needles | 60 | 58.3% | 98.3% | 24 / 0 | 1.2e-07 | 98.3% (95.0–100.0) |
| 12.5% | Doc, later turns | 60 | 50.0% | 76.7% | 17 / 1 | 0.00014 | 88.5% (79.6–98.0) |
| 12.5% | Doc, re-asked | 20 | 65.0% | 85.0% | 4 / 0 | 0.12 | 85.0% (70.0–100.0) |
| 12.5% | Every turn after turn 0 | 140 | 55.7% | 87.1% | 45 / 1 | 1.3e-12 | 92.4% (87.0–97.7) |
| 6.25% | Chat needles | 60 | 25.0% | 95.0% | 42 / 0 | 4.5e-13 | 95.0% (90.0–100.0) |
| 6.25% | Doc, later turns | 60 | 23.3% | 55.0% | 20 / 1 | 2.1e-05 | 63.5% (51.9–75.0) |
| 6.25% | Doc, re-asked | 20 | 25.0% | 60.0% | 7 / 0 | 0.016 | 60.0% (40.0–80.0) |
| 6.25% | Every turn after turn 0 | 140 | 24.3% | 72.9% | 69 / 1 | 1.2e-19 | 77.3% (70.8–84.0) |

- With dense turns, rung 5 answers 72.9%
  of turns after turn 0 at 6.25%, against 24.3%
  token by token (69 turns better,
  1 worse). Chat needles recover almost
  completely (95.0%).
- **So the remedy the data points to is not A5 as planned.** Protecting recent history would help
  chat needles but not the document, while processing a new turn with exact attention fixes most of
  both. The tier is decode-only, so it cannot do this today. A dense way for the tier to ingest a
  turn (for each layer, attend the turn's tokens over the whole layer, as tiered prefill does) is
  the candidate next item. That changes the planned direction, so it needs the owner (rule 8).
- Caveats: one model (1B), one context, one schedule, 20 sessions; the dense-turn full cache is a
  different (but also exact) feeding of the same conversation, and answers follow each policy's own
  trajectory.
